## European Cups

### Skyliners Frankfurt Suffer Third Consecutive Loss in EuroCup

Skyliners Frankfurt suffered a 113-89 defeat to Roma in their EuroCup match on Thursday. This was their third consecutive loss, following defeats in Ankara and in the Bundesliga against Mitteldeutscher BC. Despite a strong start to the season, Frankfurt struggled to contain Roma's offense, particularly in the first half, when the Italian visitors scored an impressive 64 points. The Skyliners improved in the second half, but were unable to prevent Roma from securing a convincing win. With three wins and three losses each, Frankfurt and Roma had been evenly matched in the EuroCup prior to this match.

### Rostock Seawolves Seek Fifth Consecutive Home Win

The Rostock Seawolves will host RASTA Vechta at the StadtHalle Rostock on Sunday at 15:00 in the easyCredit Basketball Bundesliga. Over 4,000 spectators are expected. Christian Held, the head coach of the Seawolves, has a personal connection to the team, having been involved with them since their promotion to the BBL in the 2021/2022 season. Held was previously the head coach of Vechta from 2020 to 2024. This will be his second time as RASTA head coach in a league game at his former workplace. Both teams have been successful in their last two games, with Rostock beating Munich and Ulm, and Vechta winning against Hagen and Chemnitz. Internationally, the Seawolves are competing in the BKT EuroCup, while Vechta is in the Basketball Champions League. In the BBL, Rostock is currently fourth with a 5-3 record, while Vechta is 13th with a 3-5 record. The Seawolves have not lost a home game in the BBL this season. Vechta had previously beaten Rostock in a preseason game in August 82-76.

### Veolia Towers Hamburg host Fitness First Würzburg Baskets in Movember match

The Veolia Towers Hamburg are set to host the Fitness First Würzburg Baskets on Saturday, November 14th, in a match that coincides with the Movember charity event. The event aims to raise awareness for prostate cancer, testicular cancer, and mental health. The Veolia Towers' Osaro Rich, who scored a personal best 16 points in the team's recent win over Jena, has been promoting the event, saying 'all mustache makes' in reference to the Movember tradition. The Fitness First Würzburg Baskets, currently seventh in the easyCredit BBL standings, have been consistent in their playing style, focusing on scoring guards and isolation plays, according to coach Filipovski. The team has also been using off-ball screens for players Jones and Griffin, a tactic they have used more prominently in recent years. The match is scheduled to start at 8pm at the Inselpark Arena, with tickets available online from €8.50.

### Oldenburg hosts ALBA Berlin in crucial BBL matchup

The EWE Baskets Oldenburg are looking to bounce back from three consecutive losses at home in the big EWE Arena, while ALBA Berlin seeks to improve its away record. The two teams have split their previous two meetings, with Oldenburg winning 74-72 in Ludwigsburg last weekend, thanks in part to Nate Johnson's 28 points and clutch free throws. Johnson, who has become Oldenburg's new top scorer with 16.3 points per game, is expected to face Jordan Ford or Jonas Mattisseck, both of whom are capable of putting up points. The game will also feature contrasting three-point shooting strategies, with ALBA taking an average of 31.9 three-pointers per game, the third-highest in the league, while Oldenburg has taken the fewest three-pointers with 22.4 per game.

### Ulm Hosts Jena in BBL Matchup with Esterkamp's Return

Steven Esterkamp returns to his former team ratiopharm ulm as head coach of Science City Jena, a team on a four-game losing streak. Jena has struggled with consistency, often losing momentum in the third quarter. In their last game, they fell to Hamburg 87-91, while ulm lost to Rostock 87-97. The matchup will feature two high-scoring players, Terrence Edwards Jr. of Jena and Jaylen Sims of ulm, who have both averaged over 16 points per game in their respective careers. Edwards has been more consistent in the BBL, averaging 13.9 points, while Sims has been working to improve his shooting percentages. The game will be a test for both teams, with ulm looking to break their losing streak and Jena seeking to turn their season around.

## Around the League

### Skyliners Frankfurt and Denis Wucherer Settle Lawsuit Out of Court

Skyliners Frankfurt and former coach Denis Wucherer have settled their long-standing dispute out of court. The parties agreed to a settlement after Wucherer was awarded 100,000 euros by the Frankfurt Labour Court in November 2025, following a ruling that his dismissal in March 2025 was unlawful. Wucherer had argued that his contract automatically extended for another year after the team secured promotion. The Skyliners had initially refused to settle, but eventually agreed to pay Wucherer the sum. The team's managing director, Gunnar Wöbke, stated that the parties had put their differences aside in the interest of resolving the matter. The settlement brings an end to a dispute that had been ongoing for over a year and a half.

### Rostock WeWolves Compete in Inclusive Basketball Tournament

The Rostock WeWolves, a team from Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, participated in the Indiwi-Inklusions-Turnier in Berlin from November 6-8. The team, led by coach Kathrin Keller, sent two teams to the tournament, with all coaches from Mecklenburg-Vorpommern working together to plan the trip. Despite several players being absent due to illness, 16 players and four coaches, including Martin Kehnscherper, Eric Lange, and Norbert Bohn, made the trip to Berlin. The WeWolves faced strong teams from across Germany, including the 2026 German champions Phoenix TSV Hagen Unified and the 2025 Landesmeister Indiwi Unified Baskets Berlin. The team struggled initially, losing to Phoenix TSV Hagen and Unified Berlin, but improved in the second half of the tournament, coming close to beating Unified Berlin in one game.

### Gladiators Trier dominate BC Batumi in Europe Cup

Gladiators Trier secured a convincing 122:57 win over BC Batumi in the Europe Cup, maintaining their perfect record in Group A. The game, played in Tiflis, Georgia, was dominated by Trier from the start, with the visitors leading 14:2 after just four minutes. The Georgians struggled to keep up, committing numerous turnovers and allowing Trier to pull away. By the end of the third quarter, Trier was ahead 94:40, and the final score was a comfortable 122:57 victory. Marco Hollersbacher and Maik Zirbes led the way for Trier, each scoring 15 points. The win sets up a busy schedule for Trier, who face Skyliners Frankfurt in the Basketball Bundesliga on Sunday.

### Hagen faces Ludwigsburg in crucial BBL matchup

Hagen is struggling at the bottom of the BBL table, having lost two games in a row, including a 74-100 defeat at home to Vechta and a 72-102 loss to ALBA Berlin. Ludwigsburg, on the other hand, is tenth in the table with two more wins than Hagen, but has also lost two games in a row. The two teams will face off in a crucial matchup, with Hagen looking to avoid falling further behind the middle of the table and Ludwigsburg seeking to maintain contact with the playoff and play-in spots. The game will feature a matchup between Hagen's Cameron Krutwig and Ludwigsburg's Thomas Rutherford, with Rutherford described as a hard worker who excels in rebounding, averaging 7.6 boards per game and ranking seventh in the league. Hagen is one of the weakest teams in the league in rebounding, averaging 34.0 rebounds per game, second only to ALBA Berlin. The two teams have a history, with Ludwigsburg winning their last matchup 88-75 on April 22, 2016.
